record.paper_title: Open Problems on Configuration Spaces of Tensegrities
record.original_question: Identify all strata of codimension greater than 1 in tensegrity configuration spaces that are not obtainable as intersections of closures of codimension-1 strata.

evidence.quote: Problem 5 Find all strata of codimension more than 1 that are not defined as an intersection of the closure of several codimension 1 strata.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$ and consider $n$ labeled points $p_1,\dots,p_n$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ (typically $d=2$). A tensegrity framework on these points with underlying graph $G$ is an assignment of a real "stress" coefficient $w_{ij}$ to each edge $\{i,j\}$ of $G$ such that the equilibrium condition
$$\sum_{j:\{i,j\}\in E(G)} w_{ij}(p_j-p_i)=0$$
holds at every vertex $i$. For a fixed graph $G$, the configuration space $\Omega_G$ is the set of point configurations $(p_1,\dots,p_n)$ that admit a nonzero self-stress, and it carries a natural stratification by the dimension of the space of self-stresses (equivalently, by the combinatorial type of the equilibrium condition). The codimension of a stratum is its codimension inside the ambient configuration space.

A stratum $S$ of codimension greater than $1$ is said to be "obtainable from codimension-$1$ strata" if there exist codimension-$1$ strata $S_1,\dots,S_k$ such that $S$ is contained in (a component of) the intersection of their closures $\overline{S_1}\cap\cdots\cap\overline{S_k}$, and equals such an intersection set-theoretically.

Problem: Identify and classify all strata of $\Omega_G$ (over all graphs $G$) of codimension strictly greater than $1$ that cannot be obtained as set-theoretic intersections of closures of codimension-$1$ strata.
artifact.status_search_result: Web search confirms this is listed among the open problems on configuration spaces of tensegrities (Arnold Mathematical Journal). No solution or partial classification of higher-codimension exceptional strata appears in subsequent literature; related progress concerns codimension-1 strata for small n and Cayley algebra descriptions, not the higher-codimension question.
